args.text:
Now, this one's a ripper. Out in a country town, there's this bloke with a weak back. Shockin' back, he reckoned. Worst back in the district.

Funny thing, but. Bet him the cigars and he'd heave a grindstone up into a farm wagon, no worries at all. Hand him an axe, though, and something'd grab him right in the spine, and in he'd go to the house for a lie-down, poor lamb. So his missus took in boarders and did all the cooking herself.

Now, fair's fair, he was happy to go halves on the work, so he did the shopping. Only, once he'd bought the tucker, he'd plonk himself down on a shoe-box with the basket between his knees and carry on that he couldn't for the life of him see what Congress was thinkin' of.

Oh, and he had theories, this bloke. Theories about the Alaskan boundary. He was dead against any Anglo-American alliance, cos Uncle Sam could look after himself at any bend in the road, when you come right down to it, and the American people were a cut above every other nationality in every way, shape, manner and form, as far as that goes. Meanwhile the missus is back home waitin', and she'd have to send word for him to get a wriggle on with the groceries so she could get the tea on.

Just about every man and his dog felt sorry for her, stuck with a great big useless lump of a husband like that. The whole town had her down as a martyr.

Then one day the husband cops sunstroke. Why? Too bone idle to shift into the shade, that's why. And the next day he carks it, without so much as an effort, which was about how he'd done everything. The widow gave him the best funeral of the year, mind you, and then every bit of folding stuff she could rake and scrape together went into a marble shaft marked "At Rest." Fair enough, too. He'd had plenty of practice.

Heaps of people said she was better off without him, and it was defo good riddance to bad rubbish.

They hoped that if she ever got hitched again she'd pick a bloke who wasn't scared of a bit of hard yakka, and had the nous to pound sand into a rat-hole.

So you can imagine, the whole town was rapt when she married Mr. Gladden, who owned the general store. And he was the real deal. He built her a brand-spankin'-new house, got a girl in to help and sent the washing out. She could stroll into the store and help herself to anything she fancied, and every evening he took her out for a spin in his new runabout.

And so, naturally, she was down in the dumps, pinin' for the jewel she'd lost. True story.

MORAL: _If the woman reckons he's all right, you keep on your own side of the fence._
